clue.text: First of various aromas swirling round boiler

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round, enclosing the single kept letter
something swirling is stirred about, so the letters of the word beside it are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, then shuffled

indicators.note: first of tells us to keep only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: opening letter of various

explanation.surface: Pleasant smells curling up around a hot-water boiler in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian urn that heats water for tea, so it is literally a kind of boiler.

clue.text: Shoot? November is not part of the season

indicators.note: if a letter is not part of a word, we take it away from that word

parts.note: one of the four seasons
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to shoot, noting November falls outside the shooting season.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the N from SPRING leaves SPRIG; the question mark flags that 'Shoot' is a plant shoot, not gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small stem or twig of a plant, which is a young shoot.

clue.text: Graduate engages someone to promote book: The Color Purple

indicators.note: to engage is to take on or hold, so the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: Master of Arts, a graduate degree
a literary agent promotes an author's book

explanation.surface: A graduate hires a literary agent to sell Alice Walker's novel The Color Purple.
explanation.walkthrough: The novel's title is redeployed as a plain description: the colour purple.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red shade, so it is a colour in the purple family.

clue.text: Watch TV that is fitted inside car

indicators.note: something fitted inside another thing sits within it

parts.note: a Volkswagen, abbreviated VW
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A television that has been installed inside a car for watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To view is what a television audience does; viewers are the people who watch programmes.

clue.text: From Hades, guilty criminal, first bum to make unwelcome appearance

indicators.note: first places this piece at the front, ahead of the rearranged letters

parts.note: bum is slang for backside

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A guilty villain bursts up from the underworld, backside first.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear its ugly head is an idiom for an unpleasant thing turning up again.

clue.text: Professor on board joined dive

parts.note: Professor Plum is a suspect in the board game Cluedo
people who have met have come together

explanation.surface: An academic who sat on a board also took a plunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' sounds like a committee seat, but the board is the Cluedo board.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply, a sudden dive downward.

clue.text: Firm reasons to support appeal for amusement park

indicators.note: in a down entry, what supports sits underneath, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a plea is an appeal
firm means sure, and reasons are grounds

explanation.surface: Solid arguments are offered to back an appeal for a theme park's planning permission.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure grounds are gardens or parks laid out for public recreation and amusement.

clue.text: Emphasise being no more than 19

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stress, as with a line drawn beneath
second meaning: below twenty, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so anything up to 19 is UNDER SCORE when the word is split.
explanation.definitionFit: To underscore is to underline, hence to stress or highlight a point.

clue.text: Am about to train extraordinary tennis player

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word before it runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports star declares she is about to do some extraordinary training.
explanation.definitionFit: Martina Navratilova and Martina Hingis are famous champions in tennis.

clue.text: Gardener returning to turn over part of the earth

indicators.note: to turn something over is to flip it, so the letters are read backwards
part says the letters are a portion of the clue's own words

parts.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A gardener comes back to dig over a patch of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' looks like the reversal signal but is just the second word holding the letters; 'turn over' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrene is an adjective meaning earthly or relating to land, from Latin terra.

clue.text: Household work our Ma managed with glee

indicators.note: managed suggests handled or arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum cheerfully got through the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: Household is not housework: Geoffrey Household wrote the 1939 thriller Rogue Male.
explanation.definitionFit: Rogue Male is the best-known novel by the author Geoffrey Household, so it is his work.

clue.text: Order court put out: resistance is much worse

indicators.note: put out means thrown out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: to direct is to order
CT is the abbreviation for court
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A judge orders the court cleared because resistance has become far worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful, so direr is the comparative: more dreadful, much worse.

clue.text: Band's number received in silence

indicators.note: received in means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to gag is to silence
N stands for number in algebra

explanation.surface: A pop group's song is met with silence by the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a band of people acting together.

clue.text: Mouthy pair regularly heard failing to offer token support

parts.note: the pair of features around the mouth

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second and fourth letters of heard
a vice is a failing or flaw

explanation.surface: A loudmouthed couple are said to be failing to back anyone properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthy' looks like cheeky, but it is just describing the pair as belonging to the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip service is support expressed in words only, without sincere action behind it.

clue.text: In base, part of chest covered in decorations

indicators.note: In tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a bed is a base, as a foundation layer
a rib bone forms part of the chest

explanation.surface: At an army base, a soldier's chest is covered in medals.
explanation.definitionFit: Beribboned means adorned with ribbons, which are decorations such as medal ribbons.

clue.text: Without transport, left out a touch

parts.note: a car is transport

indicators.note: out means removed, so this letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: -less is the suffix meaning without
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Stranded without a car, someone was left a little out of touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Without transport is CARLESS; taking out its L gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A caress is a gentle, affectionate stroke, which is a kind of touch.

clue.text: In speech demolish feeble publicity

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so we want words that sound like the answer

parts.note: to wreck is to demolish, and lame means feeble

explanation.surface: A speech that tears apart weak advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: Réclame is a French loan word in English dictionaries for publicity or self-advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclame means public attention or the art of getting it, so it is publicity.

clue.text: Transport chief hoping for donations from the passengers?

definitions.text: hoping for donations from the passengers?

parts.note: a bus is public transport
a king is a chief or ruler

explanation.surface: A transport boss passes the hat round among travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: Buskers play for coins from passers-by; the question mark admits the passers-by are here bus passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: Busking is street performing in hope of money from people going by.

clue.text: Denizens of forest run out of trousers

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so the letter is taken from the word

parts.note: breeches are knee-length trousers
R is run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Woodland creatures run off with someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Denizens' suggests animals, but the inhabitants of a forest here are trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Beeches are trees, and trees are the main dwellers of a forest.

clue.text: Massage small gap, twisting bottom

indicators.note: twisting the bottom turns round the last part of the word, swapping its final two letters

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hiatus is a gap

explanation.surface: A massage involving a little twist of the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese form of massage using finger pressure on points of the body.

clue.text: Tasteless and more than a little vulgar, is Henry

indicators.note: more than a little suggests a sizeable portion, here the back half of the word

parts.note: the final three letters of vulgar
taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry is judged tasteless and rather crude.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means gaudy and showy, which is lacking in good taste.

clue.text: Worked hard, stone split

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight of 14 pounds
riven is an old past participle meaning split

explanation.surface: A labourer toiled to break a stone in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Striven is the past participle of strive, to make great effort.

clue.text: Work by indolent author

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A book written by a lazy novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun for a book but is the verb that rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid Blyton was a prolific English writer of children's books such as the Famous Five.

clue.text: Stole whiskey — on charge

parts.note: W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rap is a criminal charge, as in rap sheet

explanation.surface: Someone nicked whisky and now faces a charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' reads as the verb steal, but it is the noun: a scarf worn over the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A stole is a long scarf or shawl, and a wrap is the same kind of garment.

clue.text: Squeeze a measure of column at foot of page

indicators.note: in a down entry, at the foot of means placed below, so this piece comes second

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for page
newspaper space is measured in column inches

explanation.surface: An editor trims a column at the bottom of a newspaper page.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is to squeeze something tightly between finger and thumb.

clue.text: Second person's half-expressed ideas

indicators.note: only half said, so just the first half of the word survives

parts.note: thoughts are ideas

explanation.surface: Someone only half says what another person is thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Thou is the old singular second-person pronoun, the equivalent of you.

clue.text: Flirt with sweetie, keeping it secret

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so one piece holds the other within
what is kept secret is tucked away out of sight inside

parts.note: hon, short for honey, is a term of endearment
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flirts with their darling but keeps the affair hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on someone is a slang idiom for making romantic advances, flirting with them.

clue.text: Public service vehicle shortly makes the side of Dutch city

parts.words: Public service vehicle shortly makes the side of Dutch city
parts.note: surface reading: a bus, abbreviated, forms part of a street or route; setter's reading: the abbreviation PSV names the football side of a Dutch city

explanation.walkthrough: PSV stands for public service vehicle, but PSV is also the football club of this city, so 'side' means a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a city in the southern Netherlands, home of Philips and its football club.

clue.text: Worked in school soundly, so covered in stars

indicators.note: soundly here means by sound, so a spoken word is matched

parts.note: studied means worked at lessons

explanation.surface: A pupil worked well and so earned plenty of gold stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'; it means 'when spoken', with STUDIED said quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Studded means dotted all over with points, as a sky or a dress may be with stars.

clue.text: Small arch, one of 5 in school

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: A little arch is one of five built in a school.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is just the number five.
explanation.definitionFit: A squinch is a small arch built across the inner corner of a square tower to carry a dome or spire.
